data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible without smuggling in induction by framing it as a non-justificatory, critical decision rule: we prefer the theory that has withstood the most severe tests not because it is more likely true or predictive, but because it is the most informative survivor of our best attempts at falsification. This preference is rational in the sense of being the outcome of critical discussion, not probabilistic inference. The cost of accepting this view is the abandonment of any rational expectation that the future will resemble the past; we act on the best-tested theory solely because it is the only one not yet known to be false, acknowledging that it may fail tomorrow just as easily as any other.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one insists that rational action requires a belief in future predictive success based on past performance, then Popper's position fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If verisimilitude (truth-likeness) cannot be meaningfully compared between false theories, the justification for preferring one over another collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distinction between 'psychological expectation' and 'methodological choice' is untenable in practice, the defense becomes purely semantic.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reframing 'preference' as a methodological rule of critical selection rather than an epistemic judgment of likelihood. The mechanism relies on the asymmetry between verification and falsification: while survival of tests does not increase probability, it does eliminate competitors, leaving the corroborated theory as the sole viable option for action until it too is falsified. This avoids induction by refusing to project past success into future reliability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
